newsitem.title: USA: Plains feedlot cattle markets quiet - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: Plains feedlot cattle markets quiet - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet with no sales reported, as packers were said to have adequate inventories following this week's active trade, feedlot sources said.

Most feedlots reported their showlists sold by midweek when packers raised bids to $72.00 per cwt, $1.00 over last week. Next week's showlists were seen unchanged to a little larger as cattle placed on feedlots last summer gradually come to market, the sources said.
Prices next week were projected steady at $72.00, unless retail demand fades and supplies expand more than expected.
Trade Friday and early next week was seen light because of the Veteran's Day holiday on Monday, with several packing plants closed, including three of 11 IBP plants.
IBP officials said the cattle plants at Amarillo TX, Emporia KS and Westpoint, Neb. would be closed Monday for the holiday, reopening Tuesday.
Excel Corp, a division of Cargill Inc, will be operating its six beef plants on Monday, according to a company spokesman.
